cve_summary: libndp before 1.6, as used in NetworkManager, does not properly validate the origin of Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP) messages, which allows remote attackers to conduct man-in-the-middle attacks or cause a denial of service (network connectivity disruption) by advertising a node as a router from a non-local network.
commit_message:
libndp: validate the IPv6 hop limit

None of the NDP messages should ever come from a non-local network; as
stated in RFC4861's 6.1.1 (RS), 6.1.2 (RA), 7.1.1 (NS), 7.1.2 (NA),
and 8.1. (redirect):

  - The IP Hop Limit field has a value of 255, i.e., the packet
    could not possibly have been forwarded by a router.

This fixes CVE-2016-3698.

Reported by: Julien BERNARD <julien.bernard@viagenie.ca>
Signed-off-by: Lubomir Rintel <lkundrak@v3.sk>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Pirko <jiri@mellanox.com>
docstring:
Summary: This function opens a raw ICMPv6 socket and configures several socket options.

Parameters: 
ndp (struct ndp *): Pointer to the ndp structure that will hold the socket descriptor.

Returns: 
int: Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

Logic: The function attempts to create a raw socket for IPv6 using the socket() function. If successful, it sets various socket options including IPV6_RECVPKTINFO, IPV6_MULTICAST_HOPS, and IPV6_RECVHOPLIMIT. If any of the socket option settings fail, it logs an error message, closes the socket, and returns the corresponding error code. If all operations succeed, it assigns the socket descriptor to the ndp structure and returns 0.
